definitions.explanation: A gift given by the hosts to guests at a wedding reception or other formal celebration as a token of thanks for attending.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧。
⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦カタログ→カタログ：10806_katarogu⟧⟦ギフト→ギフト：10824_gifuto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧だ。
examples.english: Catalog gifts are popular as wedding favors.

examples.japanese: ⟦{披露宴|ひろうえん}→披露宴：05636_hirouen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{帰|かえ}り→帰り：01275_kaeri⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧⟦{紙袋|かみぶくろ}→紙袋：09705_kamibukuro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}け{取|と}った→受け取る：01883_uketoru⟧。
examples.english: On the way home from the reception, I received a paper bag containing the wedding favor.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
At Japanese weddings, guests typically give {御祝儀|ごしゅうぎ} (monetary gifts) to the couple. In return, the couple provides {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの} to each guest. Common {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの} include tableware, catalog gifts, sweets ({引|ひ}き{菓子|がし}), and specialty food items.

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally referred to horses or other valuable items "pulled out" (⟦{引|ひ}き{出|だ}す→引き出す：03002_hikidasu⟧) and presented to guests at banquets in the Heian period.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{選|えら}ぶ→選ぶ：00835_erabu⟧ (to choose wedding favors)
- {引|ひ}き{出物|でもの}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}る→贈る：09862_okuru⟧ (to give wedding favors)
- ⟦カタログ→カタログ：10806_katarogu⟧{式|しき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{引|ひ}き{出物|でもの} (catalog-style wedding favors)
